cards.front: What is a right angle?
cards.back: A quarter turn, 90°. It looks like the corner of a book.
cards.say: What is a right angle? A quarter turn, ninety degrees. It looks like the corner of a book.

cards.front: What is an acute angle?
cards.back: An angle smaller than a right angle (less than 90°).
cards.say: What is an acute angle? An angle smaller than a right angle (less than ninety degrees).

cards.front: What is an obtuse angle?
cards.back: An angle bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line (between 90° and 180°).
cards.say: What is an obtuse angle? An angle bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line (between ninety degrees and one hundred and eighty degrees).

cards.front: How many degrees are in a straight line?
cards.back: 180°, which is a half turn.
cards.say: How many degrees are in a straight line? One hundred and eighty degrees, which is a half turn.

cards.front: How many degrees are in a full turn?
cards.say: How many degrees are in a full turn? Three hundred and sixty degrees

cards.front: Is an angle of 45° acute, right or obtuse?
cards.back: Acute, because it is less than 90°.
cards.say: Is an angle of forty five degrees acute, right or obtuse? Acute, because it is less than ninety degrees.

cards.front: Is an angle of 120° acute, right or obtuse?
cards.back: Obtuse, because it is between 90° and 180°.
cards.say: Is an angle of one hundred and twenty degrees acute, right or obtuse? Obtuse, because it is between ninety degrees and one hundred and eighty degrees.

cards.front: What are parallel lines?
cards.back: Lines that always stay the same distance apart and never meet, like railway tracks.
cards.say: What are parallel lines? Lines that always stay the same distance apart and never meet, like railway tracks.

cards.front: What is a polygon?
cards.back: A flat shape with straight sides that is closed all the way round.
cards.say: What is a polygon? A flat shape with straight sides that is closed all the way round.

cards.front: What is a regular polygon?
cards.back: A polygon with all sides equal and all angles equal, like a square.
cards.say: What is a regular polygon? A polygon with all sides equal and all angles equal, like a square.

cards.front: What is an equilateral triangle?
cards.back: A triangle with 3 equal sides.
cards.say: What is an equilateral triangle? A triangle with three equal sides.

cards.front: What is an isosceles triangle?
cards.back: A triangle with 2 equal sides.
cards.say: What is an isosceles triangle? A triangle with two equal sides.

cards.front: What is a scalene triangle?
cards.back: A triangle with no equal sides.
cards.say: What is a scalene triangle? A triangle with no equal sides.

cards.front: What is special about a rhombus?
cards.back: It has 4 equal sides, and opposite sides are parallel.
cards.say: What is special about a rhombus? It has four equal sides, and opposite sides are parallel.

cards.front: What is a parallelogram?
cards.back: A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides.
cards.say: What is a parallelogram? A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides.

cards.front: What is a trapezium?
cards.back: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.
cards.say: What is a trapezium? A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.

cards.front: What is a kite?
cards.back: A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal sides that sit next to each other.
cards.say: What is a kite? A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal sides that sit next to each other.

cards.front: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
cards.back: 5 lines of symmetry.
cards.say: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have? Five lines of symmetry.

cards.front: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
cards.back: 6 lines of symmetry.
cards.say: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have? Six lines of symmetry.

cards.front: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus (not a square) have?
cards.back: 2 lines of symmetry. They go from corner to corner.
cards.say: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus (not a square) have? Two lines of symmetry. They go from corner to corner.

cards.front: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have?
cards.back: 1 line of symmetry, from one corner to the opposite corner.
cards.say: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have? One line of symmetry, from one corner to the opposite corner.

cards.front: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle have?
cards.back: 1 line of symmetry.
cards.say: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle have? One line of symmetry.

cards.front: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram (not a rectangle) have?
cards.back: None. You cannot fold it so that both halves match.
cards.say: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram (not a rectangle) have? None. You cannot fold it so that both halves match.

cards.front: How many faces, edges and vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
cards.back: 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices.
cards.say: How many faces, edges and vertices does a square-based pyramid have? Five faces, eight edges and five vertices.
